KO.rationale: Coca-Cola's fundamental health and trajectory are genuinely strong: Q2 2026 delivered accelerating revenue (+6.7% YoY to $13.38B), expanding margins (operating margin 34.9% GAAP, 35.6% comparable), and 17% EPS growth ($1.03 vs $0.88). The franchise is executing — global unit case volume +5%, Coca-Cola Zero Sugar +16%, and management raised full-year guidance to 9-10% comparable EPS growth. Balance sheet deleveraging (equity +27% YoY to $38.31B, liabilities down to $69.61B) and 64 consecutive years of dividend increases reinforce durability. However, Pillar 2 (valuation) is the binding constraint: at 27.7x P/E with a 3.6% earnings yield versus a 4.68% 10-year Treasury, the stock has already re-rated ~3.7 turns over the past year (from ~24x to ~28x), pricing in much of the fundamental improvement. The stock sits at $88.49, just 2.7% below its 52-week high of $90.92. The 'easy' re-rating is behind. Pillar 3 offers modest support: the beat-and-raise Q2 and World Cup momentum provide near-term positive sentiment, but these are already reflected in the price move. Offsetting risks include the $14B IRS transfer-pricing exposure, the Fairlife ransomware incident, and Asia Pacific value share loss. The net assessment is a high-quality franchise that is fairly-to-slightly-rich versus its own history, with limited upside from current levels absent further earnings acceleration or rate cuts.
key_factors: Q2 2026 beat-and-raise: adjusted EPS $0.97 vs $0.93 expected; revenue $13.38B vs $13.16B expected; global unit case volume +5%; Coca-Cola Zero Sugar volume +16%; management raised FY guidance to 9-10% comparable EPS growth (from 8-9%) and ~5% organic revenue growth (from 4-5%)
Revenue +6.7% YoY ($13.38B vs $12.54B), EPS diluted +17.0% YoY ($1.03 vs $0.88), net income +16.7% YoY ($4.44B vs $3.80B) — earnings growing faster than revenue indicating operating leverage
Operating margin expanded to 34.9% GAAP (35.6% comparable) from 34.1% a year ago; net margin expanded to 33.2% from 30.3%
Balance sheet improved: total equity +27% to $38.31B, total liabilities declined to $69.61B from $74.15B, cash $13.53B; liabilities-to-equity improved from 2.46x to 1.82x
P/E diluted at 27.7x (vs 24.0x a year ago) — near upper end of 12-month range 23.2x-31.2x; multiple expanded ~3.7 turns (~15%) over the past year, pricing in much of the earnings improvement
Earnings yield 3.6% below 10-year Treasury yield of 4.68% — risk-free rate exceeds KO's earnings yield, constraining further multiple expansion
Stock at $88.49, just 2.7% below 52-week high of $90.92; +12.2% in Q2 2026 alone — near-term positive catalysts (Q2 beat, World Cup) already reflected in price
IRS transfer-pricing dispute: potential $14B incremental tax/interest exposure for 2010-2025; $6.0B already deposited; $529M reserve recorded — material contingent liability
Fairlife ransomware incident (July 16, 2026): US production temporarily suspended at high-margin dairy subsidiary; materiality not yet determined
Asia Pacific price/mix declined 9% in Q2; region lost value share in total NARTD beverages — partial offset to broadly positive share-gain narrative
Structural moat: 40% global NARTD market share, 21 billion-dollar brands, asset-light concentrate model, 64 consecutive years of dividend increases, investment-grade credit (A+/A1)
